tier_reason: README Benchmark table gives first-party compressed sizes on the 12 Silesia files for blz4 --optimal, lz4 -12 -l and lz4x -9; no timings, no compiler, flags, versions or hardware, and no benchmark script. Size-only first-party numbers are C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: No speed claim; compressed-size comparison only. blz4 --optimal is equal to or slightly smaller than lz4 -12 -l on every Silesia file (7 of 12 identical; smaller on mozilla 22,025,940 vs 22,025,988, mr 4,190,675 vs 4,190,774, nci 3,621,482 vs 3,621,567, samba 6,100,521 vs 6,100,539, xml 759,868 vs 759,901) and matches lz4x -9 exactly on every file. The README calls --optimal 'very slow' and says LZ4 is 'very close to optimal, and much faster'.

notes: Numbers check out against the README table; the record's 'most files are byte-identical' is 7 of 12. Not a speed win, kept per the seed-record rule as a size-only optimal-parse LZ4 encoder; metadata (Zlib, 28 stars, last commit 2023-11-01, stale) confirmed.

tier_reason: README gives first-party timings against zlib inflate 1.2.11 on enwik8 and a texture file, but CPU is only 'core i7', the timing compiler/flags are not given (clang 6.0.0 -O3 is stated only for the code-size table), and no benchmark harness is published.

corrections.caveats: First-party README numbers only. CPU model, compiler flags for the timing run, repeat counts and the benchmark harness are not given. Baseline is zlib 1.2.11 (2017), not a current zlib or zlib-ng/libdeflate, which are much faster than stock zlib at inflate. The README with these numbers was last updated in June 2019 ('Faster codeword reversal. Update README.'); robustness fixes followed (buffer overflow fix August 2020, merged October 2020), so the timings predate those fixes; the only 2022 commits are cosmetic (error-message style, commenting out unused code). The 'skip checksum' row does not verify integrity, so the like-for-like gain versus zlib (which verifies) is the 84%/89% row. License: zlib license, with the gzip crc32 code by Stephan Brumme under a zlib-like license, per README. Original that inflatecpp ports.

notes: All six timings match the README. Corrected the caveat that called the post-2022 commits overflow/stack fixes: those fixes are 2019-2020 and the 2022 commits are cosmetic. Metadata (80 stars, 13 forks, last commit 2022-10-12, abandoned) confirmed.

tier_reason: Wiki gives first-party times against original zlib with CPU model (i7-4702MQ) and compiler (VS 2019), and the repo ships the test application and test.sh, but optimization flags are not stated and the main datasets are the author's private files, so not A; first-party so C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Wiki Release 2 (VS 2019), level 9, C version vs original zlib: source code 5.1 s vs 10.7 s (28,858,611 vs 28,859,103 bytes); binaries 12.6 s vs 49.1 s (54,473,779 vs 54,485,836 bytes); geometry 18.2 s vs 180.0 s (114,915,875 vs 114,942,962 bytes). Wiki states the optimized version 'performs nearly 2.5-10 times faster'. Silesia (202.1 MB) level 9: 20.90 vs 8.51 MB/s; level 5: 29.82 vs 29.23 MB/s; level 1: 63.52 vs 62.10 MB/s. Derived from page data: 2.1x, 3.9x and 9.9x on the three level-9 sets, about 2.5x on Silesia level 9, about 1.02x at levels 5 and 1.
corrections.caveats: First-party numbers on an old laptop CPU (i7-4702MQ, Windows 8.1) with MSVC; the key datasets (UE4 source, binaries, geometry/textures) are the author's own and are not published, and optimization flags are not given. The gain is only at high levels: on Silesia at levels 5 and 1 it is about 2% (29.82 vs 29.23 MB/s, 63.52 vs 62.10 MB/s). Baseline is zlib 1.2.11 only; no comparison with zlib-ng, libdeflate or Cloudflare/Intel zlib forks. It replaces zlib's longest_match only; zlib 1.2.13+ removed ASMV, so it needs the bundled patch (Sources/zlib_1.2.13.patch). Compressed output is slightly smaller than stock zlib output, not byte-identical to it.

notes: All level-9 numbers match the wiki; added the Silesia level 5/1 rows that show almost no gain outside level 9. Metadata (BSD-3-Clause, 146 stars, 25 forks, last commit 2022-10-14, abandoned) confirmed.
